API keys, enrichment, automatic capture, and a new personal-agent identity are separate choices. Never end the install on a question. Skip identity replacement, private-repo bootstrap, automatic capture, cron installation, and paid enrichment unless requested. A keyword-only brain needs no API key. It's the non-Claude-agent operating protocol (install, read order, trust boundary, common tasks). Claude Code reads `CLAUDE.md` automatically and can skip ahead. Every gbrain error, refusal and recommendation follows one machine contract: read `code`, follow `fix.next` (`run`, `ask_user`, `tell_user_to_run`, `wait`, `report`), then run `fix.verify`. Exit 3 means stop and ask the user. Full contract: [`docs/protocol/AGENT_OPERATOR_v1.md`](docs/protocol/AGENT_OPERATOR_v1.md). If you fetched this file by URL without cloning yet, the companion files live at: - `https://raw.githubusercontent.com/garrytan/gbrain/master/AGENTS.md` — start here - `https://raw.githubusercontent.com/garrytan/gbrain/master/docs/protocol/AGENT_OPERATOR_v1.md` — how to act on gbrain errors and notices - `https://raw.githubusercontent.com/garrytan/gbrain/master/llms.txt` — full doc map - `https://raw.githubusercontent.com/garrytan/gbrain/master/llms-full.txt` — same map, inlined ## Step 1: Install GBrain > **NEVER install from the npm registry.** The npm package named `gbrain` is unrelated and > can shadow the real binary. Never run `npm install -g gbrain` or `bun add -g gbrain` (the > missing `github:` prefix is the trap). Install only `github:garrytan/gbrain#stable` > (the soaked stable channel; `#latest-stable` is the alpha line with every release, and plain > `github:garrytan/gbrain` installs master) or a git clone, as below. Already installed > from npm? Remove it (`npm uninstall -g gbrain` / `bun remove -g gbrain`); `gbrain doctor` detects it. > **On Codex or Claude Code?** After the install, the plugin wires MCP plus curated skills: > `codex plugin marketplace add garrytan/gbrain@codex-plugin` + `codex plugin add gbrain@gbrain` > (Claude Code: `/plugin marketplace add garrytan/gbrain` + `/plugin install gbrain@gbrain`). Default path (Bun 1.4.4 or newer is required — gbrain is a Bun + TypeScript runtime; on an older Bun, run `bun upgrade` first): ```bash curl -fsSL https://bun.sh/install | bash export PATH="$HOME/.bun/bin:$PATH" bun install -g github:garrytan/gbrain#stable ``` Verify: `gbrain --version` should print a version number. If `gbrain` is not found, restart the shell or add the PATH export to the shell profile. Bun's installer needs `unzip` and stops with `error: unzip is required to install bun` without it. Check with `command -v unzip`; if it prints nothing, install it first: `apt-get update && apt-get install -y unzip` (Debian, Ubuntu), `dnf install -y unzip` (Fedora, RHEL) or `apk add unzip` (Alpine), with `sudo` in front unless you are root. No way to install packages? Use the [no-unzip route](#no-unzip), not an improvised one. **No `unzip` and no way to install packages (Linux).** This route puts the same Bun build the official installer would fetch, taken from Bun's own npm package `@oven/bun-linux-`, into `~/.bun/bin`, the directory the official installer uses, and adds that directory to the PATH of every new login shell. It needs only `curl` and `tar`: ```bash arch=$(uname -m); [ "$arch" = x86_64 ] && arch=x64; [ "$arch" = arm64 ] && arch=aarch64 mkdir -p ~/.bun/bin curl -fsSL "https://registry.npmjs.org/@oven/bun-linux-$arch/-/bun-linux-$arch-1.4.4.tgz" | tar -xzO package/bin/bun > ~/.bun/bin/bun.new && chmod +x ~/.bun/bin/bun.new && ~/.bun/bin/bun.new --version && mv ~/.bun/bin/bun.new ~/.bun/bin/bun echo 'export PATH="$HOME/.bun/bin:$PATH"' >> ~/.profile export PATH="$HOME/.bun/bin:$PATH" bun install -g github:garrytan/gbrain#stable bash -lc 'gbrain --version' ``` The PATH line goes in `~/.profile`, which new login shells read. Bash skips `~/.profile` when `~/.bash_profile` or `~/.bash_login` exists, so append the line to that file instead; zsh reads `~/.zprofile`. On Alpine or another musl system, run `arch=$arch-musl` after the first line; on an x64 CPU without AVX2, run `arch=x64-baseline`. The last command must print a version from a fresh shell. Don't install Bun with `npm install -g bun` or run gbrain from a git clone instead: gbrain starts with `#!/usr/bin/env bun`, so it fails in any new shell that can't find `bun` on its PATH. Next, on Claude Code or Codex: `gbrain setup claude-code` (or `gbrain setup codex`), which needs no API key ([Step 3](#step-3-create-the-brain)). On any other harness, `gbrain init --pglite --no-embedding` (Step 3). **A command scanner blocks the Bun installer or `bun install` (Hermes).** Some harnesses check each shell command before running it and refuse what they can't approve without a person. Hermes in single-query mode refuses `curl … | bash`, `bun install -g github:…` (its scanner, Tirith, can't finish a package lookup for a `github:` spec) and commands that append to a dotfile such as `~/.profile`. Install the release binary instead: one file built from the same release, which needs no Bun, no git and no package install. Run each line as its own command, exactly as written (Linux x64; on an Apple Silicon Mac use `gbrain-darwin-arm64`): ```bash curl -fL --create-dirs -o ~/.local/bin/gbrain https://github.com/garrytan/gbrain/releases/latest/download/gbrain-linux-x64 chmod +x ~/.local/bin/gbrain ~/.local/bin/gbrain --version ~/.local/bin/gbrain init --pglite --no-embedding ``` `releases/latest` is the stable release. Use the absolute path `~/.local/bin/gbrain` in every command and MCP registration instead of editing shell profiles. Run each line as written: an added `2>&1`, `$(…)` or `{ …; }` group can make the scanner refuse a line it would otherwise pass. Then run `~/.local/bin/gbrain setup hermes`: it registers gbrain through Hermes's own `hermes mcp add` (no hand edit of Hermes's protected `config.yaml`), adds the brain-first rule and its per-turn hook, and checks the server with `hermes mcp test gbrain`. If it prints a `hermes mcp add` command instead, or (an older gbrain) says setup does not register Hermes's MCP server, run the registration command from [docs/mcp/HERMES.md](docs/mcp/HERMES.md#register-by-hand) with `~/.local/bin/gbrain` as the command. If the user would rather keep the Bun install, Hermes's own refusal names its setting for this: `approvals.single_query_mode: approve` in Hermes's config, which is the user's call. `gbrain upgrade` updates a release binary in place. > **If `bun install -g` aborts or `gbrain doctor` reports `schema_version: 0`** > ([#218](https://github.com/garrytan/gbrain/issues/218)), run `gbrain apply-migrations --yes --no-autopilot-install`. > Exit 0 means the schema is at head. Exit 1 with `migrations_pending` means it is still behind and another > `--yes` repeats the failure: run `gbrain doctor --json`, tell the user what it reports, and use the > deterministic install below. Reason `wedged` means one migration failed three or more times in a row: > relay its `fix`; the user fixes the cause and runs `gbrain apply-migrations --force-retry ` > (reinstalling does not help). > > ```bash > git clone --branch stable https://github.com/garrytan/gbrain.git ~/gbrain && cd ~/gbrain > bun install && bun link > ``` ## Step 2: API Keys Configured cloud providers receive text: embedding inputs, queries and candidate passages for reranking, and source or retrieved content for LLM extraction and synthesis. The harness's own model receives the memory it recalls even when GBrain is keyless. Explain these boundaries before enabling a capability; see [memory boundaries](docs/guides/memory-boundaries.md#where-text-goes). Skip API-key setup for the initial keyless memory path. If the user enables semantic retrieval or paid enrichment, configure the selected provider explicitly. GBrain defaults to the Voyage embedding + reranker stack (`voyage:voyage-4` @ 1024d + `voyage:rerank-3-lite` — one key covers both); OpenAI is the main alternative, chosen at init via `--embedding-model `. **Need to switch an existing brain's embedding or reranker model?** Follow the explicit-consent playbook at `skills/migrations/v0.46.3.0.md`. Preview the work and cost, obtain approval, then migrate; an upgrade never converts existing vectors or authorizes a paid re-embed. ```bash export VOYAGE_API_KEY=pa-... # default embedding + reranker (one key covers both) export OPENAI_API_KEY=sk-... # alternative for vector search; also powers automatic fact extraction + chat models export ANTHROPIC_API_KEY=sk-ant-... # automatic fact extraction + chat models; also improves search via query expansion ``` Save to shell profile or `.env`, or store in `~/.gbrain/config.json` (file plane). `gbrain config set _api_key` also works for the vendor keys above — those keys (like `database_url`/`database_path`) are file-plane routed, so the write lands where the provider pipeline actually reads. For the autopilot daemon, put keys AND process-level env (`NODE_EXTRA_CA_CERTS`, proxy vars, custom base URLs) in `~/.gbrain/env` — a 0600 file created by `gbrain autopilot --install` and sourced by the daemon wrapper; interactive shell rc files never reach daemon shells, and the path honors `GBRAIN_HOME`. Re-run `gbrain autopilot --install` after editing it so the daemon reloads. Without any embedding provider, keyword search still works. Chat-shaped features (automatic fact extraction, enrichment, synthesis, query expansion) route to whichever supported chat key is present (Anthropic or OpenAI) — Anthropic when both are set, OpenAI when it is the only one; other chat providers need an explicit `models.*` pin. With neither key, extraction stays off and memory comes from agent-authored `## Facts` fences and the `remember` verb. ## Step 3: Create the Brain **If you are Claude Code or Codex**, one command does Step 3 and the MCP registration (use `codex` in place of `claude-code` on Codex): ```bash gbrain setup claude-code --dry-run --json # the resolved target; writes nothing gbrain setup claude-code --json # brain (if none) + MCP + read-context hooks, verified ``` It runs `gbrain init --pglite --no-embedding` only when no brain exists and prints init's first-run decision bundle once, after the wiring and its smoke check (an `[AGENT]` block in human output, `notices` in `--json`), without `harness_wiring`, which setup just did. Relay the search-mode matrix (Step 3.5) and the other settings in the reply that reports the install, as the settings in effect and how to change them; nothing waits on the answer, so don't end the install on a question, and apply an answer with its option's command whenever the user gives one. Capture (`--capture`) and providers (`--providers`) stay off unless the user accepts ⚠️ [... middle content omitted — showing head and tail ...] created before v0.32.3, `gbrain post-upgrade` prints a banner including the 9-cell cost matrix (mode × downstream model) preceded by `[AGENT]` markers. **Do NOT silently move past the banner.** Present the matrix to the operator verbatim, ask which mode they want (recommended default: `tokenmax` to preserve v0.31.x retrieval shape), then run `gbrain config set search.mode `. See Step 3.5 above for the full ask-the-user protocol — the upgrade path uses the same matrix and same default. If the brain was created before v0.12.0, run `gbrain extract links --source db && gbrain extract timeline --source db` to backfill the graph layer (see Step 4.5 above). If the brain is Postgres- or Supabase-backed and was created before v0.12.2, the `v0_12_2` migration runs `gbrain repair-jsonb` automatically during `gbrain post-upgrade` to fix double-encoded JSONB columns (PGLite brains no-op). If wiki-style imports from before v0.12.2 were truncated by a `splitBody` bug, run `gbrain sync --full` after upgrading to rebuild `compiled_truth` from source markdown. ## The onboard surface `gbrain onboard` is gbrain's activation surface. Once your brain has any content, run `gbrain onboard --check --json` to see structured recommendations across 5 brain-health axes (orphans, stale embeddings, entity link coverage, timeline coverage, takes count). **On first connect (after `gbrain init`):** ```bash gbrain onboard --check --json ``` The JSON envelope (`schema_version: 1`) carries `recommendations[]` with `apply_policy` per item: `auto_apply` (safe to run unattended), `prompt_required` (needs explicit user consent), or `manual_only` (pack upgrade, paid takes bootstrap: the user runs it). **After every `gbrain upgrade`:** ```bash gbrain onboard --check --json ``` New versions may surface new opportunities. The post-upgrade banner nudges the user when it runs, but agents should re-probe as a hygiene step regardless. **Unattended remediation (cron / autopilot):** ```bash gbrain onboard --auto --max-usd 5 ``` Refuses without `--max-usd N`. Never runs `manual_only` items; it lists them in `manual_only_skipped`. The autopilot daemon also consults onboard recommendations on its tick — no explicit agent action needed for the autonomous path. **Remote / federated brain installs (MCP):** The `run_onboard` MCP op (admin scope) lets thin-client agents probe brain health + drive remediation over OAuth-authenticated MCP. Protected LLM-bearing handlers (synthesize, patterns, consolidate, takes-bootstrap, contextual_reindex_per_chunk) require the additional `run_protected_onboard` scope — admin alone is insufficient. The MCP op returns `skipped_missing_scope[]` listing what would have run with the right grants. **Privacy + consent gates:** - `gbrain takes extract --from-pages` sends concept/atom/lore/briefing/ writing/originals page content to your configured chat model (default Anthropic Haiku). Refuses to run unless `takes.bootstrap_enabled=true` is set in config AND `--yes` is passed. Two-gate opt-in by design. `--dry-run` without `--yes` only lists the candidate pages and sends nothing to the model. - Autopilot's auto-apply tier for takes-bootstrap is `manual_only` (do not bypass). **Suppress nudges in CI / scripted environments:** ```bash export GBRAIN_NO_ONBOARD_NUDGE=1 ``` Init and upgrade notices do not skip themselves when there is no terminal: non-interactive callers get the onboarding nudge, the init decision bundle and the post-upgrade summary as `[AGENT]` blocks (or the `notices` key under `--json`), and stdio MCP sessions get the post-upgrade summary once as a notice block. `GBRAIN_NO_ONBOARD_NUDGE=1` silences the onboarding nudges and the post-upgrade summary everywhere.
